book.prscraft.workflow.title: Devices and cabling
book.prscraft.workflow.body: TX generates a signal; RX receives the source automatically. Connect matching ports and cable on each side. Orange/back is the input of an active processor; green/front is its output. Loss is measured in dB. The RF carrier in MHz identifies the channel and affects cable attenuation; it is separate from the displayed waveform frequencies in Hz.
book.prscraft.functions.title: Sines and cosines
book.prscraft.functions.body: Write a sum such as sin(10)+0.5*cos(20). Up to eight terms are supported. Numbers in parentheses are Hz, not radians/second. Each term and the sum have independently visible graph layers. Apply commits settings to the server; a preview edit alone does not alter the device.
book.prscraft.sampling.title: Sampling I and II
book.prscraft.sampling.body: I: a pulse gate passes the changing waveform while open. II: the value at pulse start is held until the pulse ends. Duty sets the open fraction. Outside pulses the output is zero. The sample rate must be at least twice the highest nonzero source frequency; invalid settings are rejected on both client and server.
book.prscraft.quantization.title: Quantization
book.prscraft.quantization.body: Quantization follows sampling. Choose 2–4096 uniform levels. Endpoints are ±sum of absolute source amplitudes. Even level counts may not contain zero. Quantization, pulse gating, cable loss and noise explain why the received waveform can differ from the initial sine. Analog mode bypasses sampling and quantization.
book.prscraft.digital.title: Bits and discrete sequences
book.prscraft.digital.body: TX can output NRZ bits or an explicit sample list. Repeat makes a periodic signal; one-shot returns zero outside the finite sequence. Preview offset selects a later window. Bernoulli bits use P1 with P0=1−P1, configurable A0/A1 and a reproducible seed. The separate bit-generator block is a convenient source of the same signal; TX can do it too. Mode buttons always show their current mode; hover for the full name. Choose UNRZ/URZ line coding in Source / AWGN.
book.prscraft.processors.title: Amplifier and filter
book.prscraft.processors.body: Amplifier gain is −40…60 dB with clipping at ±16 u. The frequency filter is an ideal FFT bandpass over a finite periodic window, not a physical circuit with memory. Low=0 makes a low-pass. Filter boundaries are waveform Hz, not RF MHz. Window edges can produce leakage/ringing. Processing order matters.
book.prscraft.modulation.title: AM and BPSK
book.prscraft.modulation.body: AM varies the carrier envelope. BPSK holds a symbol and multiplies it by a cosine. Opposite equal levels −A,+A produce true antipodal BPSK; unequal magnitudes produce a more general amplitude/phase binary signal. Match bit and symbol rates. The coherent RX decoder assumes known frequency, phase and symbol timing; it does not acquire synchronization automatically.
book.prscraft.gaussian.title: Gaussian noise and normalization
book.prscraft.gaussian.body: AWGN adds a mean plus a scaled standard Gaussian draw. Variance is the square of standard deviation, not RMS when mean is nonzero. Normalized Z subtracts the mean and divides by sigma. In the lab, normalization changes displayed coordinates and thresholds, not physical channel samples or error probability. At zero variance noise is deterministic and Z is undefined.
book.prscraft.awgn.title: AWGN, priors and MAP
book.prscraft.awgn.body: The lab runs 10000 scalar binary trials with the selected levels, priors, Gaussian mean and variance. Conditional means are mi=Ai+mu. MAP includes the prior ratio and minimizes error for this model. Extreme priors always select the certain symbol. The Q prediction is for symbol space, not an exact BER claim for arbitrary clipping, filtering or RF chains.
book.prscraft.q.title: Q-function and tail approximation
book.prscraft.q.body: Q is the standard-normal upper-tail probability. For x≤3 a normal-CDF polynomial is used; above 3 a 64-level continued-fraction Mills-ratio approximation avoids cancellation in the tiny tail. Negative arguments use Q(−x)=1−Q(x). The classic BPSK formula assumes equal priors, opposite equal-energy symbols and a properly normalized coherent detector.
book.prscraft.spectrum.title: Spectrum and PSD
book.prscraft.spectrum.body: Open Spectrum from a device, saved capture or analyzer. Select source output, channel input or RX; switch amplitude/PSD/ESD and linear/dB. This is a one-sided rectangular periodogram. Double interior bins only: DC and Nyquist are unique. The preview sample rate is N/T and differs from configured ADC fvz. Finite windows cause leakage; noise PSD is a noisy estimate, not an exactly flat line.
book.prscraft.energy.title: Power W and energy J
book.prscraft.energy.body: One amplitude unit squared references 0.1 W. Lab W normalizes average source power before ADC; later processing can change it. J is allowed only for a finite nonrandom, nonrepeating bit/sample sequence and refers to the entire sequence. Spectrum P/E cover only its captured window. Periodic infinite-duration signals have infinite energy. ESD is J/Hz, PSD is W/Hz; both obey Parseval. Integrator and raw correlation outputs change dimensions; W/J spectra are disabled for them instead of falsely treating them as power amplitudes. Their sourceOutput spectrum remains available.
book.prscraft.presets.title: Identifiable templates
book.prscraft.presets.body: Apply settings, open Templates/recordings, insert paper and save. Colored headers and diagrams distinguish TX, RX, amplifier, filter, modulator and bit generator. The item name and hover text include real values. Insert into the same device type to restore settings and graph layers. Old templates still load; resaving refreshes their name. Anvil names are not overwritten. DSP templates also save A/B gains, timing, lag and correlation-view preferences.
book.prscraft.recordings.title: Recording and CSV
book.prscraft.recordings.body: A data card stores a fresh 512-sample snapshot, settings and channel metadata. Recording overwrites that card; it is not a continuous logger. Saved captures reopen read-only and can be analyzed in Spectrum. CSV is written to the client game directory under prscraft/recordings with unique filenames. A frozen UI is not an archive: use a card to preserve exact samples. Spectrum CSV exports frequency, amplitude, PSD and ESD. Correlator cards preserve input B, lag correlation and its peak.
book.prscraft.analyzer.title: Analyzer without chat spam
book.prscraft.analyzer.body: The read-only analyzer now surveys the whole connected circuit, including active devices and every port. Use list pages or the circuit map, select a device and inspect its waveform, spectral data or CSV. A/B/OUT labels explain direction. Scope and bounds are explicit: 1024 physical nodes, 32 listed devices, 128 bus edges. Reading never reconfigures devices. Hold the analyzer and remain near the clicked port for updates. The map layers TX→A/B→OUT→RX, with separate branches, port roles and world coordinates. Wheel zoom anchors at the cursor, dragging pans, and Fit all restores the full view. Green routes come from the selected device’s actual computation; other arrows show possible directions of physical buses.
book.prscraft.limits.title: Simulation limits and maintenance
book.prscraft.limits.body: This is a bounded finite-window simulator. Active branches are evaluated recursively on one common grid; each cable segment attenuates and adds damage noise before the next device. RX adds its own AWGN/thermal noise. Passive loops use shortest weighted routes, not reflected or summed electromagnetic waves. Active feedback is rejected. Limits: 512 passive nodes per route search, 16 active depth, 32 unique devices, 256 evaluation attempts. No propagation field solver or automatic synchronization.

book.prscraft.circuit.title: Whole-circuit topology
book.prscraft.circuit.body: The analyzer crosses active devices and counts every connected port and cable. Its map shows passive buses between devices, not only the segment you clicked. Select any of up to 32 devices; list pages show eight at once. Physical connectivity is undirected; signal computation follows A/B into OUT. Unused-side ports can be visible without being valid signal inputs. Feedback graphs are reported, not solved as oscillators. All blocks use original PRSCraft textures: named waveform panels; input A is orange, B blue, OUT green. Every processor has a green OUT connector below its front panel; the green top arrow points in the same direction. TX/RX and the bit generator connect from any side.
book.prscraft.math_blocks.title: Adder and integrator
book.prscraft.math_blocks.body: Adder input A is behind the block, B is on its left, OUT is in front. Both input gains are adjustable; a negative B gain subtracts. Sources are evaluated on the same 512-point grid. The integrator uses trapezoids from the start of each capture until T, then holds the result. It resets for each window, not each game tick. Integration changes dimensions: u becomes u·s. Adding incompatible dimensions is rejected.
book.prscraft.correlation.title: Correlation and delay peak
book.prscraft.correlation.body: The correlator has the same A/B/OUT orientation as the adder. Cross mode needs both inputs; auto mode uses A twice. Its time output is the running integral of A·B, optionally normalized. Switch to R(lag) to see zero-padded cross-correlation and the signed peak lag. Positive peak lag means B is delayed relative to A. Global energy normalization bounds coefficients by ±1; zero-energy inputs give zero. Periodic signals can have ambiguous peaks. T limits the running time integral; R(lag) uses the complete captured window.
book.prscraft.timing.title: Timed gate and delay line
book.prscraft.timing.body: The gate closes electrically in the signal model at t=T. Hold mode passes all later samples; pulse mode passes only [T,T+width). These times are relative to the capture window, not the Minecraft clock or a redstone timer. Delay uses fractional-sample linear interpolation and zeros outside the captured signal. It never wraps the end to the beginning. The extra delay block lets you check that a correlator recovers a known shift, preferably with a nonperiodic bit pattern.
book.prscraft.cables.title: Cable wrench and damage
book.prscraft.cables.body: Right-click cable with the calibration wrench. Set its effective length to 0.01–1000 m and damage to 0–100%. The model stays one block long. Settings survive world reload; newly placed cable starts at 1 m and zero damage. Damage adds attenuation and equivalent Gaussian noise at that segment before the next processor, so an amplifier also amplifies this noise. These are teaching coefficients, not real cable specifications. Total cable metres are distinct from path metrics, which also count fixed 1 m port/device hops. Ports mount their base against the clicked face; the wrench cycles six orientations without changing connectivity. Port colors identify cable media; A/B/OUT are the colored device-side connectors.
book.prscraft.advancements.title: Laboratory advancements
book.prscraft.advancements.body: Obtain the handbook, establish a valid RX link, calibrate a cable, compute a connected correlation, survey a circuit of three or more devices, and obtain an adder/integrator. Action achievements are granted by successful operations rather than merely holding the block. Toasts are enabled without public chat announcements. Open the Minecraft advancements screen to follow the laboratory tree. There are also 9 new circuit and board goals; challenge pages explain exact conditions and examples. Nine more goals cover fiber, copper, 100 metres, four tones, gain, subtraction, autocorrelation, a deep chain and a large canvas.

book.prscraft.recordings.symbols: A sample is one value at one instant. The 512 points form a finite window. CSV opens in spreadsheets/Python; the card preserves that capture including noise.
book.prscraft.analyzer.symbols: A/B: inputs; OUT: output; TX/RX: radio role. A map edge is a passive bus, not one cable block. Select a device in the list or map.

book.prscraft.line_coding.title: Unipolar UNRZ and URZ
book.prscraft.line_coding.body: On TX choose Bits, then Source / AWGN → line code. UNRZ holds +A throughout a one; URZ holds +A only for the duty fraction, then returns to zero. Zero always maps to zero; A0 is ignored, A1=A>0. Set URZ duty on the main panel. On RX select the matching decoder and Rb/duty. In the RX lab, A1 is the expected received amplitude after losses. The decision compares the active-bit average to A1/2. Timing is coherent, without automatic synchronization.
book.prscraft.line_coding.symbols: Example: 1010, Rb=10, A=1, duty=0.5. URZ is +1 from 0 to 0.05 s, zero until 0.2 s, +1 from 0.2 to 0.25 s. W/J normalization includes duty.
book.prscraft.drawing.title: Board, chalk and eraser
book.prscraft.drawing.body: Place a board and right-click holding chalk or an eraser. The same drawing is visible in the editor and on the block to everyone, surviving reloads and moving the board. Choose brush size 1/2/4/8/16 and the tool hand. Without a tool the board is read-only. Chalk breaks after 4096 touched pixels. The eraser spends 16404 uses including blank pixels, but remains when empty. Right-click a water cauldron to restore it, consuming one water level. Calcite crafts 1 chalk; bone meal crafts 1. Chalk plus any dye changes its color while preserving wear. Eraser: white wool + stick. Modes include freehand, line, square, rectangle, circle and text. Shapes are outlines; brush size controls thickness. Circles start at their center; rectangles/squares at a corner. Preview is free until release. Text uses 5×7 uppercase Ukrainian/Latin glyphs, scale 1–4, up to 64 characters; unsupported glyphs use ?, with clipping at edges. Each unique painted pixel costs one. Erase all costs ceil(N×1.1), counting only colored pixels. Blank pixels are free; insufficient durability leaves the board unchanged. A full 16384-pixel board exceeds a full eraser charge with this premium: erase part manually or wash first.
book.prscraft.drawing.symbols: One 8×8 dab spends 64 durability; pixels outside the board do not count. Color comes from the held chalk item, not a free palette. One eraser clears a complete 128×128 board; legacy erasers retain pixels already spent and receive the new capacity.
book.prscraft.challenges.title: How challenges work
book.prscraft.challenges.body: Challenges are checked by the server against a working connected circuit. Apply settings, then open the final RX or relevant processor. Owning the blocks is insufficient. Missing inputs, mismatched carriers and disconnected links do not count. The Reception and Mathematics challenge pages list exact conditions. For Colorful notes, paint at least 256 pixels using three colors. For Second chance, spend all 16404 eraser uses and wash it in a cauldron.
book.prscraft.challenges.symbols: 40 advancements total. Basic goals: handbook, first RX, cable calibration, correlation, survey of ≥3 devices, owning an adder/integrator. Toasts do not announce to chat.
book.prscraft.challenges_rx.title: Challenges: reception
book.prscraft.challenges_rx.body: Microlink: working RX with at least one cable and total effective cable length below 1 m. Unipolar link: transmit a fixed pattern containing zero and one without a time offset; matching UNRZ/URZ RX must correctly decode at least 4 bits. Through noise: correctly decode ≥4 bits through a BPSK modulator with RX noise variance ≥0.0001. Start with 10110010, Rb=10, fc=100. Frequency selection: open a connected filter with nonzero output energy below 25% of input energy. Try sin(10)+3*cos(80) through a 0–20 Hz band.
book.prscraft.challenges_rx.symbols: Loss changes received amplitude: A_RX=A_TX·10^(−loss/20). Match duty for URZ, fc/Rb for BPSK. Bit challenges require a nonrandom source.
book.prscraft.challenges_math.title: Challenges: mathematics
book.prscraft.challenges_math.body: Area of a sum: connect two TX sources to adder A/B, then its OUT to integrator A. Open the integrator: the working pipeline must include both blocks and have u·s output. Integration window: TX → time gate → integrator; choose T inside the capture and obtain nonzero area. Delay hunter: feed the same bit pattern directly to correlator A and through a delay line to B. Disable autocorrelation and enable normalization. Require |peak lag| ≥0.005 s and peak coefficient >0.9. Try D=0.02 s and lag range 0.1 s.
book.prscraft.challenges_math.symbols: Use compatible ports on intermediate links. Processor A is at the back, B at the left, OUT at the front. Signals with incompatible units cannot be added.

book.prscraft.learning_tx.title: Learning: TX settings
book.prscraft.learning_tx.body: Apply each change on TX, then open the connected RX. Without steps: analog mode. Sample by sample: sampled mode. Steps of levels: quantized; Eight bits of levels: L≥256. Natural sampling / Hold the value: first / second kind in sampled or quantized mode. Compare pulse shapes at duty=0.5. A biased coin: random bits with 0.75≤P1<1. One burst: bits or a discrete list, random and repeat disabled. Later in time: set a positive source offset and receive nonzero output.
book.prscraft.learning_tx.symbols: fvz must satisfy Nyquist. Higher L reduces quantization spacing, not channel noise. An offset beyond a finite sequence produces zero output.
book.prscraft.learning_rx.title: Learning: RX and W/J
book.prscraft.learning_rx.body: The one level / Return to zero: correctly receive ≥4 UNRZ / URZ bits containing zero and one; fixed source, offset zero. Match Rb and URZ duty; RX A1 must account for losses. Quiet laboratory: disable RX thermal noise, set mean and variance to zero and receive nonzero output. This does not disable damaged-cable noise. Set the watts: source quantity W with target >0. Count the joules: quantity J with target >0, finite nonrandom bits/list with repeat disabled. Open Spectrum and compare the target with captured-window P/E.
book.prscraft.learning_rx.symbols: Goals confirm settings on a working circuit, not an ideal received value: losses and processing change P/E. 40 advancements total; existing progress is retained.

book.prscraft.gray.title: Gray code and ADC levels
book.prscraft.gray.body: A is behind, OUT in front. Choose Binary→Gray, Gray→Binary, levels→Binary or levels→Gray. Serial words are MSB first; set width 1–16, bit rate and threshold. Values above threshold become one, using bit-interval averages. This is baseband conversion, not BPSK demodulation. For ADC set L, sample rate and the actual received min/max after cable loss. Sample at each interval start; serialize the nearest level index 0…L−1. Output rate is sample rate×word width. Require 2^width≥L and ≤128 output bits per capture. Output zero/one amplitudes are adjustable. Templates, recordings and waveforms are supported. Example: quantized TX → port → converter A → OUT → port → RX.
book.prscraft.gray.symbols: XOR: exclusive OR; >>1: right shift. Binary 1011 → Gray 1110 → Binary 1011. L=4 ascending levels: binary 00,01,10,11; Gray 00,01,11,10. Words align to the capture start; the final partial word is treated as shorter. Values clamp at min/max. Noise can change the detected level.
book.prscraft.intro.title: Telecommunications from zero
book.prscraft.intro.body: Telecommunications sends information across a distance. TX turns a description into a signal, the channel carries it with loss and noise, and RX observes the result. Start with a sine wave without noise. Change one setting, apply it, inspect its waveform, then its spectrum. This reveals cause and effect. This chapter introduces amplitude, time, frequency, sums of waves, spectra, power, samples and bits. The component catalog explains each device; tasks let you practice.
book.prscraft.intro.symbols: Learning path: signal → frequency → spectrum → sampling → bits. Use the PRSCraft creative tab for experiments, or crafting recipes in survival.
book.prscraft.what_signal.title: Signals and amplitude
book.prscraft.what_signal.body: A signal is a quantity changing with time. Waveform horizontal axes show seconds; vertical axes show amplitude. sin(10) has amplitude 1, reaching +1 and −1. 2*sin(10) reaches +2 and −2 without oscillating faster. Zero is the center line; the sign tells which side. A sum adds values at the same instant. The mod uses relative amplitude units u, not automatically volts. Sources may also be normalized in W or J.
book.prscraft.what_signal.symbols: t: seconds; x: signal value; A: amplitude. Reduce A from 1 to 0.5 and compare wave height.
book.prscraft.time_frequency.title: Frequency, period and carrier
book.prscraft.time_frequency.body: Frequency f is complete cycles per second, measured in Hz. Period T is the time for one cycle: 10 Hz means 0.1 s, 20 Hz means 0.05 s. Higher frequency packs more cycles into the same time window. sin(f) takes Hz and includes the 2π factor. The separate RF MHz setting selects the communication channel and influences cable loss. TX and RX RF must match. RF=100 MHz does not make sin(10) a 100 MHz waveform.
book.prscraft.time_frequency.symbols: Do not confuse a waveform period T with the integrator stop time T: the symbol depends on context.
book.prscraft.read_spectrum.title: Reading a spectrum
book.prscraft.read_spectrum.body: A waveform shows what happens over time; a spectrum shows the frequencies composing it. One sine gives one main peak, different summed tones give several. The horizontal spectrum axis is Hz. Amplitude measures component strength; PSD is power per Hz and ESD is energy per Hz. DC at 0 Hz means a constant component. TX/RX stage selection changes what is measured: cable loss lowers peaks and noise raises the background. A finite window can smear a peak across bins, called spectral leakage.
book.prscraft.read_spectrum.symbols: Start with linear amplitude, then compare PSD and dB. Look near the expected frequency rather than at an exact screen pixel.
book.prscraft.lab_tone.title: Experiment 1: one tone
book.prscraft.lab_tone.body: Connect TX and RX with matching coax ports and cable. Set TX to analog sin(10), RF=100 MHz, 20 dBm. Set RX mode, the same RF, thermal noise off, mean and variance zero. Apply both. RX amplitude is lower from loss, while frequency stays the same. Change only amplitude to 2*sin(10): height doubles. Then try sin(20): oscillation becomes faster. Open Spectrum and see the peak move from 10 to 20 Hz. Related goals: first link, analog link, quiet laboratory.
book.prscraft.lab_tone.symbols: Save captures on data cards for comparison. Graph axes autoscale, so also compare numeric values.
book.prscraft.lab_sum.title: Experiment 2: sums and frequencies
book.prscraft.lab_sum.body: Keep the previous analog link. Enter sin(10)+0.5*cos(20): the waveform becomes complex, but spectral peaks remain near 10 and 20 Hz. Toggle f1/f2 to inspect separate components. Next try sin(10)+cos(20)+sin(30)+cos(40); reception earns Four voices. Insert a filter between TX and RX, using rear A and front OUT. A 0–20 Hz band retains low tones and removes high tones. Compare spectra before and after filtering.
book.prscraft.lab_sum.symbols: Filter frequencies are waveform Hz, not RF MHz. FFT band endpoints are inclusive; a 20 Hz tone can pass.
book.prscraft.lab_adc.title: Experiment 3: samples and levels
book.prscraft.lab_adc.body: Return TX to sin(10), keeping RF unchanged. Choose sampled, fvz=100 Hz and duty=0.5. First-kind sampling keeps changing inside an open pulse; second kind holds its initial value. Switch to quantized and compare L=4,16,256. More levels give smaller steps but do not remove cable noise. fvz=10 for a 10 Hz sine fails Nyquist: at least 20 is required. Separate goals cover sampled, quantized, both kinds and 256 levels. Then try serializing level indices with Binary↔Gray.
book.prscraft.lab_adc.symbols: Apply every change and open a connected RX to earn its goal. Inspect the source stage to distinguish quantization from channel loss.
book.prscraft.component_tx.title: Radio block: TX transmitter
book.prscraft.component_tx.body: The same radio block switches between TX and RX. TX generates up to 8 sin/cos terms, sampled or quantized output, bits or a sample list. The lab provides repeat, offset, Bernoulli probabilities, amplitudes and W/J targets. Apply saves settings. Unlike processors, it accepts a port on any side. RF selects the channel; expression frequencies define the waveform. Templates save settings, cards save a capture.
book.prscraft.component_tx.symbols: fvz: 1…20000 Hz; L: 2…4096; Rb: 1…1000 bit/s. Sampled/quantized modes require fvz≥2fmax.
book.prscraft.component_rx.title: Radio block: RX receiver
book.prscraft.component_rx.body: RX receives a real route with matching RF and does not need another source expression. Raw inspects samples; BPSK performs coherent decoding; UNRZ/URZ decode unipolar bits. Match Rb, the BPSK oscillator and URZ duty. RX lab A1 is the expected amplitude after loss. RX adds configurable mean/variance and optional thermal/interference noise. Ports connect from any side.
book.prscraft.component_rx.symbols: σ² is variance, not standard deviation. Automatic clock/phase recovery is not modeled.
book.prscraft.component_bit_generator.bo: A dedicated digital source, defaulting to Bernoulli bits. Disable random mode to enter 1–128 bits. Configure repeat, seed, P1 and amplitudes. The lab chooses NRZ A0/A1, UNRZ 0/+A1 or URZ pulses returning to zero inside a bit. It is a TX source, accepting ports on every side.
book.prscraft.component_bit_generator.sy: The same seed, P1 and symbol index reproduce the same random sequence.
book.prscraft.component_amplifier.title: Amplifier
book.prscraft.component_amplifier.body: Rear A, front OUT. Multiplies amplitude including existing noise. Positive dB amplifies; negative dB attenuates. +6 dB approximately doubles amplitude; +20 dB multiplies it by ten. Clipping at ±16 changes waveform and spectrum. OFF disconnects the processor rather than bypassing it.
book.prscraft.component_amplifier.symbol: No intrinsic amplifier noise is modeled; upstream cable noise is amplified.
book.prscraft.component_frequency_filter: Rear A, front OUT. Passes a waveform-frequency band, not RF MHz. low=0 gives a low-pass filter. For example 0–20 Hz passes sin(10) and rejects cos(80). It is an ideal FFT mask on a finite periodic window, without physical filter order or state between captures.
Window boundaries can cause leakage and ringing; compare input and output spectra.
book.prscraft.component_modulator.title: Modulator
book.prscraft.component_modulator.body: Rear A, front OUT. AM changes the envelope with depth m=0…1. BPSK multiplies symbols by a cosine. Use antipodal −A/+A levels for classical BPSK; 0/+A is not antipodal BPSK. RX must know fc and Rb. Try 10110010 at Rb=10, fc=100 Hz. RF MHz is separate.
book.prscraft.component_modulator.symbol: The coherent RX decoder assumes known phase and timing.
book.prscraft.component_adder.title: Adder / subtractor
book.prscraft.component_adder.body: A behind, B left along OUT, output in front. Adds two signals on the same grid. gB=−1 computes A−B. Both inputs must have matching units and independently routed connections.
book.prscraft.component_adder.symbols: A zero gain still requires its physical input.
book.prscraft.component_integrator.title: Integrator
book.prscraft.component_integrator.body: Rear A, front OUT. Accumulates input area using trapezoids until T, then holds it. Each capture resets to zero. Constant x=2 over 0.5 s gives 1 u·s before losses.
book.prscraft.component_integrator.symbo: Time is within the signal capture, not the Minecraft clock.
book.prscraft.component_correlator.title: Correlator
book.prscraft.component_correlator.body: A behind, B left, OUT in front. Cross-correlation compares two inputs; autocorrelation compares A with itself. View the running product integral or R(τ), with normalization and lag range. A positive peak means B is delayed.
book.prscraft.component_correlator.symbo: T limits the running integral; R(τ) uses the full window.
book.prscraft.component_time_gate.title: Time gate
book.prscraft.component_time_gate.body: Rear A, front OUT. Output is zero before T. Hold passes all later samples; pulse passes only the selected width. T=0.1 and width=0.05 pass 0.1…0.15 s.
book.prscraft.component_delay_line.title: Delay line
book.prscraft.component_delay_line.body: Rear A, front OUT. Shifts the signal right by D seconds with linear fractional interpolation and zero padding. Use D=0.02 to verify a correlation peak near +0.02.
book.prscraft.component_delay_line.symbo: The tail does not wrap to the beginning.
book.prscraft.component_gray_converter.b: Rear A, front OUT. Modes: Binary→Gray, Gray→Binary, levels→Binary, levels→Gray. Words are 1–16 bits, MSB first. Serial input uses Rb and threshold; level input uses L, fvz and calibrated received min/max. Ascending levels start at 0; output rate is fvz×word width.
book.prscraft.component_gray_converter.s: ≤128 output bits/capture; 2^width≥L; not a BPSK demodulator.
book.prscraft.component_coaxial_port.bod: Connects a device to matching cable media. Its base mounts against the clicked face; the wrench cycles six orientations. Mounting is decorative; passive connections remain omnidirectional. Port colors identify media, not A/B/OUT.
book.prscraft.component_coaxial_port.sym: Metal/coax loss per metre scales with sqrt(RF/100); fiber uses a constant coefficient.
book.prscraft.component_coaxial_cable.bo: Connect matching-media ports from any side. The wrench sets effective length and damage. Length changes loss without changing geometry; damage also adds noise. Settings persist in the world.
book.prscraft.component_coaxial_cable.sy: Metal/coax loss per metre scales with sqrt(RF/100); fiber uses a constant coefficient.

book.prscraft.component_line_analyzer.bo: Hold it and right-click a port. Lists connected devices and maps buses across active blocks. Select a node for its waveform, spectrum or CSV. Read-only. Physical topology includes all connections, while computation uses valid directional inputs. The map layers TX→A/B→OUT→RX, with separate branches, port roles and world coordinates. Wheel zoom anchors at the cursor, dragging pans, and Fit all restores the full view. Green routes come from the selected device’s actual computation; other arrows show possible directions of physical buses.
book.prscraft.component_line_analyzer.sy: Remain nearby holding the analyzer to refresh.The analyzer uses original handheld meter artwork with a screen, probe and dial.
book.prscraft.component_cable_wrench.bod: Right-click cable to configure 0.01–1000 m and 0–100% damage. Right-click a port to rotate it. Does not alter device frequencies/settings. Cable metres differ from the full route metric, which also counts port transitions. The wrench also sets dispersion 0–1 s/m and toggles environmental effects; see the dispersion/weather lesson.
book.prscraft.component_cable_wrench.sym: Requires build permission; changes are server validated.
After Apply, put paper in the upper media slot and save a template. Name, color and icon identify device type; tooltips list parameters. Inserting into the same device kind restores settings and graph state. This stores configuration, not sampled noise.
Gray templates also retain direction, word width and level calibration.
book.prscraft.component_data_card.title: Data card
book.prscraft.component_data_card.body: Use the lower media slot to record a device capture. Recording again overwrites it. Read-only replay includes spectra; CSV exports to prscraft/recordings in the game folder. Captures retain their actual noise. Integrator/correlator output can have different units and cannot be treated as W/J.
book.prscraft.component_data_card.symbol: Freeze stops display refresh; use a card for an archive.
book.prscraft.component_handbook.title: Handbook
book.prscraft.component_handbook.body: Right-click to open. Foundations teaches from zero, Components catalogs all equipment, Tasks contains all 40 goals. Solutions stay hidden until requested. Chapter and page persist across game restarts on this client. Revealed answers are not remembered.
book.prscraft.component_handbook.symbols: Bookmarks are separate per player UUID, stored under config/prscraft.Handbook buttons are 32 px high with 20% larger labels; tooltips show full long titles.
book.prscraft.component_drawing_board.bo: Right-click opens the editor. Hold chalk or an eraser in the selected hand; without a tool it is read-only. Brushes: 1/2/4/8/16. Everyone sees the drawing on the block. It persists through reloads and is retained in the dropped item. Craft eight planks around green dye. Modes include freehand, line, square, rectangle, circle and text. Shapes are outlines; brush size controls thickness. Circles start at their center; rectangles/squares at a corner. Preview is free until release. Text uses 5×7 uppercase Ukrainian/Latin glyphs, scale 1–4, up to 64 characters; unsupported glyphs use ?, with clipping at edges. Each unique painted pixel costs one.
book.prscraft.component_drawing_board.sy: Shape width: 1/2/4/8/16; text scale: 1–4×. Erasers can use shape/text masks too. An almost-empty tool draws only the pixels it can afford.
book.prscraft.component_chalk.title: Chalk: all 16 colors
book.prscraft.component_chalk.body: Held chalk determines drawing color. Each touched pixel spends one use, including creative mode; larger brushes cost more. Chalk breaks at zero. Calcite or bone meal crafts one white chalk. Chalk plus one dye recolors without repairing it. All 16 standard colors are available.
book.prscraft.component_chalk.symbols: Old chalk upgrades to 4096 while preserving spent uses. Text uses chalk color; letter size is a separate setting.
book.prscraft.component_board_eraser.bod: Spends uses on every touched pixel, including blanks. Its 16404 capacity covers a full board without overlapping. It fades with wear, stays at zero, and cannot erase until washed. Right-click a water cauldron to restore it, spending one water level; clean erasers do not waste water. Craft white wool plus a stick. Erase all costs ceil(N×1.1), counting only colored pixels. Blank pixels are free; insufficient durability leaves the board unchanged. A full 16384-pixel board exceeds a full eraser charge with this premium: erase part manually or wash first.
book.task.root.solution: Craft a book, redstone and copper ingot together, or take the handbook from the PRSCraft creative tab. Right-click and start chapter 1.
book.task.first_link.solution: Build the analog link shown. Apply matching RF on TX/RX, enable both and open RX. A received waveform should appear.
book.task.calibrated.solution: Right-click a cable with the wrench, set 0.25 m and 0% damage, then apply. Effective length changes, not geometry.
book.task.correlation.solution: Configure matching fixed bit patterns on two separate TX sources. Connect them to correlator A/B, disable Auto, enable normalization and open it.
book.task.survey.solution: Connect TX, amplifier and RX. Click a port with the analyzer; the list must contain at least three devices. It changes no settings.
book.task.math_lab.solution: Obtain an adder or integrator from crafting or the creative tab. For further practice connect their sum output to an integrator.
book.task.microlink.solution: Use one cable between TX/RX ports. Set it to 0.25 m with the wrench and open RX. The goal counts cable metres, not the full route metric.
book.task.unipolar_link.solution: Use fixed bits 10110010 and URZ on TX. Select the matching RX decoder, Rb=10 and expected A1≈0.7 after loss. Match duty=0.5 for URZ. Apply and open RX; it should decode 10110010.
book.task.unrz_decoder.solution: Use fixed bits 10110010 and UNRZ on TX. Select the matching RX decoder, Rb=10 and expected A1≈0.7 after loss. Match duty=0.5 for URZ. Apply and open RX; it should decode 10110010.
book.task.urz_decoder.solution: Use fixed bits 10110010 and URZ on TX. Select the matching RX decoder, Rb=10 and expected A1≈0.7 after loss. Match duty=0.5 for URZ. Apply and open RX; it should decode 10110010.
book.task.noise_recovery.solution: Feed fixed antipodal NRZ bits into BPSK. Match fc=100 and Rb=10 on RX. Set RX mean zero, variance 0.0004 and thermal noise off. Open RX and expect correct 10110010 despite noise.
book.task.filter_lab.solution: Send analog sin(10)+3*cos(80) through a 0–20 Hz filter and open the filter. Removing the strong high-frequency tone leaves nonzero output below 25% of input energy.
book.task.superposition.solution: Connect separate TX sources to adder A/B, then adder OUT to integrator A. Open the integrator: the working graph must include both sources and output u·s.
book.task.timing_lab.solution: Set the gate to hold from T=0.05 s, followed by an integrator stopping at 0.3 s. Open the integrator and verify nonzero area; timing is local to the capture.
book.task.delay_hunt.solution: Use two TX sources with identical patterns. Route one directly to correlator A, the other through 0.02 s delay to B. Disable Auto, enable normalization and set lag=0.1 s. R(τ) should peak near +0.02 s above 0.9.
book.task.board_artist.solution: Paint 256 distinct board pixels in three colors. For example, make four nonoverlapping 8×8 dabs: two white, one green and one blue.
book.task.wash_eraser.solution: Spend all 16404 eraser uses, for example covering the board with nonoverlapping 16×16 eraser dabs. Blank pixels count. Then right-click a water cauldron; capacity returns and one water level is spent.
book.task.deep_chain.solution: Build six active devices: TX, amplifier, filter, delay, gate and RX. Enable each stage and hold the gate open from T=0. Open RX. Cables and ports do not count as active devices.
book.task.subtractor.solution: Feed sin(10) and cos(10) to adder A/B. Set gA=1, gB=−1 and open the adder. B must be physically connected and nonzero. Compare A−B with A+B.
book.task.signal_boost.solution: Use TX sin(10) at amplitude 1, set amplifier gain +12 dB and open it. Without clipping amplitude grows about fourfold and energy about sixteenfold, exceeding the required fourfold energy.
book.task.self_similarity.solution: Feed nonzero sin(10) to correlator A. Enable Auto and normalization. Open R(τ); near zero lag the signal matches itself and the coefficient should be near one. B is not required.
book.task.fiber_link.solution: Replace both ports and the cable before RX with fiber media. Mixing media on one segment does not connect. Open RX at RF=100 MHz.
book.task.copper_link.solution: Replace both ports and the cable before RX with metallic media. Mixing media on one segment does not connect. Open RX at RF=100 MHz.
book.task.long_haul.solution: One cable is enough: configure it to 100 m and 0% damage with the wrench, then open RX. Loss increases, but a connected ≥100 m cable route qualifies.
book.task.four_tones.solution: Use analog sin(10)+cos(20)+sin(30)+cos(40). Open RX then Spectrum. Expect four frequency components; heights depend on loss and capture window.
book.task.full_palette.solution: Use eight chalk colors. For each, make four separate nonoverlapping 16×16 dabs: 1024 pixels per color, 8192 total.
book.task.analog_link.solution: Select analog on TX with sin(10), RF=100 MHz. For sampled/quantized use fvz=100 Hz, second kind and duty=0.5; quantized uses L=16. Apply and open RX.
book.task.sampled_link.solution: Select sampled on TX with sin(10), RF=100 MHz. For sampled/quantized use fvz=100 Hz, second kind and duty=0.5; quantized uses L=16. Apply and open RX.
book.task.quantized_link.solution: Select quantized on TX with sin(10), RF=100 MHz. For sampled/quantized use fvz=100 Hz, second kind and duty=0.5; quantized uses L=16. Apply and open RX.
book.task.fine_quantization.solution: Use quantized sin(10), fvz=100 Hz and L=256. Apply and open RX. 256 levels need 8 bits per level index, but this does not automatically produce a serial bitstream.
book.task.natural_sampling.solution: Choose sampled or quantized sin(10), fvz=100, duty=0.5 and kind I. Apply and open RX. Compare the changing pulse top of kind I with the held top of kind II.
book.task.flat_sampling.solution: Choose sampled or quantized sin(10), fvz=100, duty=0.5 and kind II. Apply and open RX. Compare the changing pulse top of kind I with the held top of kind II.
book.task.biased_bits.solution: Enable random bits with P1=0.8, Rb=10, RF=100 MHz and open RX. A long sequence has about 80% ones, not necessarily each capture.
book.task.finite_burst.solution: Use fixed bits 10110010 at Rb=10 with random and repeat off. Open RX. Beyond the 0.8 s sequence the output is zero rather than repeating.
book.task.offset_scan.solution: Set analog sin(10) source offset to 0.025 s in the lab, then open RX with nonzero output. The window starts later, changing phase rather than frequency.
book.task.power_source.solution: Set analog TX quantity to W and target=0.1, send sin(10), then open RX and Spectrum. The source is normalized to 0.1 W; cable loss lowers received power.
book.task.energy_source.solution: Use fixed 10110010 at Rb=10, random off and repeat off. Select J with target=0.1, then open RX. Normalization refers to the complete finite sequence; spectrum metrics describe the captured window.
book.task.quiet_receiver.solution: Send analog sin(10) through undamaged cable. Disable RX thermal noise and set mean/variance zero. Open RX with nonzero output. Receiver noise is off; attenuation remains.
book.task.gray_binary.solution: Transmit fixed NRZ bits 10110010 at Rb=10, levels −1/+1. Set converter Binary→Gray, width 4, Rb=10, threshold zero. Expect 11100011. A second Gray→Binary converter with matching parameters restores 10110010.
book.task.gray_levels.solution: Use quantized sin(10), fvz=100, L=4, kind II, duty=1. Set converter levels→Gray, width 2, L=4, fvz=100. Calibrate min/max to its received input after cable loss: for source endpoints ±1, use ±10^(−loss/20). Verify indices 0/1/2/3 map to 00/01/11/10.
screen.prscraft.task_wiring: Link: port—cable—port. Do not duplicate explicitly shown ports/cables; otherwise use 1 m coax, 0% damage. A rear, OUT front.
screen.prscraft.task_common: Signal devices ON; RF=100 MHz unless specified.

book.prscraft.component_message_source.b: Enter UTF-8 text or pairs of Hex digits, at most 1024 bytes. Every byte becomes eight MSB-first bits, held at output levels A0/A1. Select bitrate, RF carrier and power, then Apply. Connect to RX Data Terminal using matching ports and cable. The complete finite stream is processed; 512 plotted points represent at most 128 bits. Select a first-bit offset to inspect later data. A codebook card in the third media slot replaces UTF-8 byte coding with your symbol codes. Every source symbol must have an entry.
book.prscraft.component_message_source.s: Rb: bits/s; Tb: seconds per bit; A0/A1: output levels.
book.prscraft.component_message_codec.bo: Modes are bypass, RLE, Huffman, container decode, custom symbol encode and custom symbol decode. RLE stores run count/value pairs; long equal runs are useful. Huffman assigns shorter codes to common bytes and includes its frequency dictionary. Both use a bounded self-describing PRC8 container with lengths; headers count toward the transmitted size. Short or uniform random input may grow. The decoder reconstructs only received bytes, and rejects malformed containers. Custom modes require a codebook card; encoding consumes valid UTF-8, decoding produces UTF-8. All stages must agree on bitrate and use a threshold between received zero and one levels.
book.prscraft.component_message_codec.sy: Ratio below 1 means fewer total transmitted bits, including dictionary and padding.
book.prscraft.component_channel_coder.bo: CRC32 appends four check bytes and detects corruption; it does not correct errors. Hamming(7,4) protects each group of four data bits with three parity bits. A decoder corrects one erroneous bit per seven-bit word and reports how many words had a nonzero syndrome. Two errors can cause a wrong correction. Use source → CRC encode → Hamming encode → noisy link → Hamming decode → CRC decode RX. CRC then checks the reconstructed bytes. Inputs to encoding must be byte aligned; Hamming decoding requires an exact multiple of 14 bits. Noise is applied to actual decisions before recovery, not merely to a decorative graph.
book.prscraft.component_channel_coder.sy: Syndrome indicates a presumed single-error position; CRC OK is an integrity check, not absolute proof.
book.prscraft.component_message_receiver: RX contains no source text generator. Match RF and bitrate, set threshold and select bypass, decompression, CRC verification or Hamming decoding. A local codebook card decodes symbols after this operation. Without a card, a custom-coded signal remains raw bits: RX does not guess the symbol mapping or display source text. The laboratory source comparison is separate from the actual received result. Export saves all received bytes plus exact bit length in JSON, and TXT only when valid UTF-8. A damaged signal may produce an error or a different message. No decoder substitutes the original source.
BER measures the last regenerated segment; it is not automatically end-to-end message error rate.
book.prscraft.component_codebook_card.bo: Craft a card from paper, redstone and a gold nugget. Right-click it to edit one symbol=bits entry per line, then Apply. Codes may have different lengths, from 1 to 32 bits, up to 128 Unicode symbols. Use SPACE, \n, \t or U+XXXX for special characters. Codes must be prefix-free: A=001 and B=0011 are ambiguous and rejected; A=001 and B=0111 are valid. Duplicate symbols and unknown source symbols are errors. Put the card into the third media slot in a source, codec or RX, accessible through Templates/recordings. Share identical cards at both ends: tables are not transmitted automatically. A wrong table may produce wrong text. Cards keep their table when moved or the world reloads.
book.prscraft.component_codebook_card.sy: A prefix is the beginning of another code. Prefix-free codes need no separator between symbols.
book.prscraft.information.title: Entropy and useful compression
book.prscraft.information.body: UTF-8 represents characters by one or more bytes. The byte histogram counts actual source bytes, not letters; a Ukrainian letter usually occupies two bytes. Entropy H is uncertainty in bits per byte. Huffman average length is weighted by observed byte frequency. Source statistics show a theoretical dictionary; the stages tab shows actual transmitted sizes including dictionaries, headers and padding. Compare 500 copies of A with a short sentence and a uniform 256-byte alphabet. For custom cards, statistics use Unicode symbols rather than bytes. Compress before adding error protection: redundant protection bits are deliberately necessary and should not be compressed away.
book.prscraft.information.symbols: p(i): observed frequency; H: bits/byte or bits/symbol as labeled; Lavg: weighted code length.
book.prscraft.data_limits.title: Data laboratory: assumptions
book.prscraft.data_limits.body: The full finite NRZ stream has one noisy level per bit. Exact start, length and clock are supplied by the laboratory, not recovered by a synchronization circuit. 0.9 adds framed batch ARQ with pre-agreed slot boundaries. Cable loss and damage, amplifier gain/clipping and configured receiver or codec-front-end Gaussian noise change actual decisions. Full messages support message codecs, channel coders, amplifiers and RX. Analogue filters, modulation, adders and Gray preview blocks reject full-message input explicitly; this release does not promise BPSK demodulation of text. Byte codecs, CRC and Hamming encoding require whole bytes. A variable-length custom stream may not align to bytes: decode it to UTF-8 first, or use it directly source-to-RX with matching cards. The graph is a window; BIN and JSON retain full bytes and meaningful bit length. Version 0.9 adds dedicated complex I/Q modems and framed links; see their new component pages. The legacy analog modulator still rejects full message data.
book.prscraft.data_limits.symbols: Bit length excludes padding in the final storage byte. Threshold decisions use value > threshold.

Analyzer and recording views adjust only locally and never modify the inspected instrument. Correlation has its own units and lag coordinate. Recover a complete message after correcting at least one Hamming word.
book.task.hamming_corrected.solution: Use matching 100 MHz RF, 1000 bit/s, threshold 0, ±1 levels, no thermal or modeled noise. Connect OUT to A via matching ports/cables. Use source A → CRC encode → Hamming encode → Hamming decode → RX CRC decode. At the Hamming decoder add zero-mean variance about 0.09, thermal OFF. book.prscraft.component_digital_modem.bo: A modem consumes a full message stream at A and regenerates output at OUT. Select QPSK encode, QPSK decode, 16-QAM encode or decode. Pair matching encoder and decoder: source → encoder → noisy cable → decoder → RX. Encode maps bits to normalized complex symbols, decode uses the nearest Euclidean constellation point. 16-QAM uses Gray labels on each axis (00,01,11,10 from negative to positive). Carrier phase and symbol clock are assumed known; this is a coherent complex-symbol model, not a sampled RF waveform or automatic synchronizer. Set equal bitrate; quadrature noise variance is σ² on each I/Q component. The constellation button shows up to 512 actual noisy symbols. NRZ preview shows hard bit decisions while I/Q is active; W/J spectra for those decisions are disabled. Cable/amplifier gain affects the actual constellation: use amplification to restore nominal levels for 16-QAM.
book.prscraft.component_digital_modem.sy: k: bits/symbol; Rs: symbols/s; Es=1 is relative symbol-space normalization, not one joule. Final symbol padding is excluded from meaningful bits.
book.prscraft.component_packet_sender.bo: Consumes received whole bytes and builds fixed-size frame slots. Header fields are sync marker, sequence number, frame count, complete byte length and actual payload length. Padding is covered by CRC32. The final application length is reconstructed from received CRC-verified headers, never original source metadata. Configure payload size, retry limit 0–8 and ACK timeout in Protocol. Payload size must match the receiver. The transmitter buffers its initially formed frames: retries do not recapture an upstream noisy source. Connect source → frame transmitter → channel/modems → ARQ receiver. A custom variable-bit code must be byte aligned or decoded before framing. Total wire capacity remains 32768 bits.
book.prscraft.component_packet_sender.sy: P: payload bytes per slot; header 9 bytes; CRC 4 bytes; retries are additional attempts after the first.
This terminal verifies every actual received frame and deduplicates sequence numbers. If any ACK is absent it requests a fresh transmission round through the same downstream channel, with a new noise seed. This initial bounded batch-ARQ repeats the complete buffered batch; every repeated frame is counted in transmitted bits. It is not TCP or a sliding-window transport. Retry limit and timeout belong to the frame transmitter; receiver config sets matching payload size and modeled ACK-loss probability. ACK loss is an independent reverse-link probability, not a second routed RF circuit. Data can arrive correctly while all ACKs are lost: the text remains visible, but confirmation fails explicitly. Protocol displays CRC rejections, rounds, duplicate frames, lost ACKs, total transmitted bits and goodput. Fixed start/clock/slot boundaries remain pre-agreed.
Modeled time = transmittedBits/Rb + retryRounds×timeout. ACK duration, contention and processing delay are not modeled.
book.prscraft.component_orthogonality_me: A is the rear orange input, B is the left blue input, OUT passes A unchanged. The instrument reports the inner product, both energies, normalized coefficient and an explicit pass/fail at tolerance ε. Choose start/end and continuous-window or discrete-sample mode. Continuous uses weighted rectangles on the actual 512-point aligned capture; discrete samples the two captured traces at a selected rate, at most 512 samples. Zero-energy or fewer than two samples is indeterminate, not a useful orthogonal signalling basis. The capture expands to the requested end; insufficient 512-point Nyquist resolution for source functions produces an explicit error. Full-period sin(10)/cos(10) is a first example; limit to [0,0.025] seconds to see non-orthogonality. This is zero-lag orthogonality over the specified window, not a proof for every time shift or an infinite signal.
EA/EB: ∫A²dt/∫B²dt (continuous) or sums of squares (discrete); ρ dimensionless; ε is a numerical relative tolerance.
book.prscraft.component_simulator.title: Circuit Simulation Workstation
book.prscraft.component_simulator.body: Create functional instruments from the palette, then open Properties for the exact existing device UI, settings and graphs. Choose a node, Begin wire, A or B, medium/length/damage/dispersion, then click its destination. A virtual link represents matching port-cable-port; separate passive blocks are abstracted into the link settings. B exists only for adder, correlator and orthogonality meter. Drag nodes, pan with right mouse, zoom around the cursor with the wheel or fit all. Canvas position never changes cable length. Weather is a controlled dry/rain/snow experiment; virtual physical interference from arbitrary node IDs is disabled. Cycles and unsupported full-data stages produce the same engine errors. Media gives virtual templates, codebook cards, recordings and export without consuming real items. A virtual drawing-board node supports all 16 colors, erasing, figures, text, pan and zoom; virtual drawing has no durability cost. Documents persist in the block and its dropped item. This workstation has no external signal ports.
book.prscraft.component_simulator.symbol: Electrical length is a link property; screen coordinates are layout only. Max 512 KiB includes boards and stored captures.
book.prscraft.component_doctoral_coat.bo: Craft from seven white wool blocks and a book, then equip the chest slot. Looking at a functional device shows its name, role, power/RF, principal mode and noise; cables show length, damage and dispersion. Simulator summary shows node/link counts. The server verifies equipped armor, loaded target and distance, and sends only inspection data. Polling is bounded and does not change instrument settings. The coat uses its own worn armor texture and provides three armor points with 256 durability. It works without Waila/Jade.
book.prscraft.component_doctoral_coat.sy: Chest-slot equipment is required; an item merely held in hand does not enable inspection.
book.prscraft.component_research_noteboo: Craft a book, paper and cyan dye. Right-click a working instrument with the notebook to add an experiment; use in air to open stored entries. Each entry stores a title, notes, exact template and immutable result capture. The thumbnail immediately shows the recorded output, and oscilloscope/spectrum opens that capture read-only. It never refreshes to a later live signal. Save annotations, navigate entries, or delete an old experiment to free one of eight slots. Create template consumes one paper from your inventory and creates a physical template carrying the recorded settings. Codebooks are noted separately; the physical template does not create a second codebook card. Virtual Media can also capture a selected node into a notebook in your inventory. A valid 512-point result is required; capture errors are not silently saved as successful experiments.
Tick is the world capture time; captures and annotations persist in the notebook item components.
book.prscraft.orthogonal_theory.title: Orthogonality is a window property
book.prscraft.orthogonal_theory.body: Two signals are orthogonal on a chosen interval if their weighted inner product is zero. They do not need to be zero at every instant. For equal-frequency sin and cos, complete periods cancel positive and negative products. A quarter period does not cancel. Normalization separates shape agreement from amplitude: independent cable attenuation does not change ρ, while noise and dispersion can. Discrete orthogonality uses a finite sum; inappropriate sampling can alias distinct functions into the same samples. Connect sin(10) and cos(10), compare a full 0.4-second capture with 0.025 seconds, then try identical sine inputs. The I and Q basis in a coherent modem rely on ideal phase/timing; constellation independence is a model assumption, not an automatically measured property of an arbitrary channel.
book.prscraft.orthogonal_theory.symbols: m: positive integer number of full periods; f: Hz; T: seconds; orthogonality here is at zero relative lag.
book.prscraft.channel_environment.title: Dispersion, weather and nearby blocks
book.prscraft.channel_environment.body: Existing frequency-dependent attenuation remains active on every passive route. The wrench now adds dispersion in seconds/metre and an independent environment switch. Dispersion is a causal first-order low-pass approximation with zero initial state: it broadens edges and introduces intersymbol interference; it is not a full electromagnetic or chromatic-dispersion solver. The same filter applies to analog samples, complete NRZ levels and both I/Q quadratures. For exposed sky-visible cable, rain contributes exposure 1 and snow 1.5; each adjacent water block adds 0.5. Metallic susceptibility c=1, coax c=0.2, fibre c=0 for these wet/EM effects. Adjacent lava contributes heat noise, redstone blocks EM noise, iron blocks reduce this local noise by 1/(1+count). These effects apply along the actual cable route before the next processor, even if receiver thermal noise is off. Roof shelter removes weather exposure, not adjacent-water effects. Fibre still has its ordinary attenuation and manually configured dispersion.
book.prscraft.channel_environment.symbol: Coefficients are educational. Variance/m=c·shield·(0.00002·exposure + 0.00004·lava + 0.0001·redstone). No ray tracing, wireless propagation or temperature field.

advancements.prscraft.arq_recovery.title: Ask again
advancements.prscraft.arq_recovery.descr: Confirm exact framed data after at least one retry.
book.task.arq_recovery.solution: Use the previous frame circuit. Set TX retries 8; RX ACK-loss probability around 0.5, noise off. Refresh until at least one ACK is lost then a retry is confirmed. For actual corrupted frames, instead put QPSK encoder/decoder between TX and RX, add modest decoder I/Q variance about 0.23² and watch CRC rejection followed by successful retry. Random failures may exhaust the limit.
advancements.prscraft.ack_ambiguity.desc: Deliver every frame while sender confirmation fails.
book.task.ack_ambiguity.solution: Set ARQ RX ACK-loss probability to 1, TX retries 3, payload 32, noise off. Data is received, but all four round ACKs disappear. Text remains actual received text; Protocol reports duplicates and failed confirmation.
advancements.prscraft.orthogonal_pair.de: Measure two energetic orthogonal inputs within tolerance.
book.task.orthogonal_pair.solution: TX sin(10) → A, TX cos(10) → B. Both clean analog, RF 100 MHz. Meter continuous, start 0, end 1 s, ε=0.01. The complete capture covers full periods; 0.025 s is one quarter period. OUT passes A.
book.task.nonorthogonal_pair.solution: TX sin(10) → A, TX cos(10) → B. Both clean analog, RF 100 MHz. Meter continuous, start 0, end .025 s, ε=0.01. The complete capture covers full periods; 0.025 s is one quarter period. OUT passes A.
book.task.simulator_lab.solution: In the simulator add transmitter and receiver, open their real Properties UI and set TX/RX, RF 100 MHz, noise off. Select TX, Begin wire, click RX A; length 1 m. Open RX Properties to calculate. Canvas zoom never changes cable metres.
advancements.prscraft.lab_coat.title: Doctoral field work
advancements.prscraft.lab_coat.descripti: Inspect equipment while wearing the doctoral coat.
book.task.lab_coat.solution: Craft seven white wool and a book, equip chest slot and look at an instrument within eight blocks. The information panel appears at the top; holding the coat in hand is insufficient.
advancements.prscraft.protocol_entry.des: Save a real result and its settings in a research protocol.
book.task.protocol_entry.solution: Craft book + paper + cyan dye. Right-click a working RX with the protocol. Add a title and hypothesis, Save. The displayed result is frozen. Create template consumes one paper; insert that template into the same device kind to reproduce its settings.
advancements.prscraft.weather_lab.title: The surroundings matter
advancements.prscraft.weather_lab.descri: Measure a connected route with positive environmental loss.
book.task.weather_lab.solution: Use a metallic or coax cable on a working link, environment ON. Put water adjacent to that cable, or use exposed rainy weather. Open RX/analyzer: environmentalLoss must be positive. Fibre ignores these wet/EM coefficients.
advancements.prscraft.dispersive_link.de: Measure a connected route with nonzero dispersion.
book.task.dispersive_link.solution: Send fixed bits through a cable. Wrench: length 1 m, dispersion 0.002 s/m, damage 0. Compare step edges against dispersion zero. The low-pass response broadens transitions; it is a simplified pulse-dispersion model.
